item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 4 November 2026
item.description:
Syp is ready for a full WoW Forever month, with side helpings of LOTRO and cozy hibernation energy for the rest of November.

Tipa digs Guild Wars 2’s big Vloxx dilemma but says the god-fight mechanics are a miserable slog, even if the story setup is fun.

Cliffski breaks down Ridiculous Space Battles’ tiny £915.20 budget, with stock assets and AI art/voice doing a lot of the heavy lifting.

Frostilyte recaps an October derailed by Steam Next Fest and reviews, then makes time to rave about Well Dweller’s everything-clicks appeal.

Heartless says Mistfall Hunter weirdly makes fantasy extraction plus Souls-like combat click, with tense loot runs and fights that feel worth taking.

Bhagpuss is intrigued by Silver Palace’s Victorian-anime-gacha genre blender, even while suspecting the detective angle could be the catch.

Marc looks back at the Wii’s launch by tracing Nintendo’s shaky pre-2006 position and how different the company’s fortunes feel now.

Wilhelm finds Over the Hill’s Asgard Mountain a real difficulty spike, full of icy trails, winch saves, and plenty of tumbling off cliffs.

Tobold recommends Frosthaven Digital in story mode, arguing the relaxed resting rules make its brutal card-timer tactics finally fun instead of maddening.

UltrViolet celebrates a rare good Commanders week, then wrestles with moving his AI fantasy league off ChatGPT to a local Antigravity setup.

Dave Winer celebrates Atlantis getting Frontier’s debugger back, which matters because he builds and tests code right inside it.

Cristian argues France’s proposed per-GB internet tax hits content providers first, but streaming, games, and subscription prices would likely feel it next.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 3 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae stumbles through a busy Divinity: Original Sin 2 ship chapter with teleport pyramids, inventory chaos, a bone spider, and one endangered black cat.

Kimimi finds Bangai-O Spirits fascinating but exhausting, with puzzle-heavy stages, fiddly weapon choices, and DS-screen chaos making Treasure’s challenge feel a bit woolly.

Margot’s week is all about handheld anticipation, backlog reality, Caravan SandWitch plans, and mixed feelings on Gloomy Eyes’ clunky puzzles.

David’s Dragonbane crew pushes deeper into Gunderholfen’s Level 5, mapping tight corridors, dodging suspicious levers, and promptly attracting a giant spider.

Wilhelm heads into EVE Online low-sec with the Imperium’s pirate-themed Siseide deployment, hauling his ancient Archon and spotting some jump-fatigue slapstick en route.

Roger revisits classic Tom Baker-era Doctor Who, praising Gothic horror, Gallifrey politics, Davros, and some surprisingly creepy robots and monsters.

Bhagpuss finally circles back to TV after a Suno-fueled detour, squeezing in Doctor Who, The Boroughs, and Deadloch around weather and dog care.

Joel rounds up an October heavy on gaming and reading, with Dune Messiah and Battle Angel Alita standing out from a packed media month.

Tan’s week mixes pumpkins, kids, a magical first kingfisher sighting, and more Symphony of the Night alongside Aristotle chat.

Ramen Junkie uses AI for blogging plumbing, not prose, from migrating WordPress to Hugo to automating Joplin posts and quick banner creation.

Dave Winer talks through a better web for writers while juggling Atlantis, Bonbon, FeedLand, and the ongoing hunt for a proper debugger.

Emily lays out why managed WordPress suits a hobby writer better than self-hosting: less PHP panic, fewer maintenance chores, more actual writing.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 2 November 2026
item.description:
Azuriel finds Enshrouded 1.0 neither quite Valheim nor quite action RPG, but 30 hours later he’s mostly won over despite the constant base-hopping friction.

Mailvaltar checks in on Neverness to Everness 1.4, liking Blackbird’s Salem-style story less than the band drama around Akane and Lines.

Shintar pokes at retail WoW leveling, arguing freer zone scaling helps but empty worlds and weak quest XP still make the journey feel off.

Wes spotlights the long, very human fan-translation saga behind The Legend of Xanadu, with 15 years of hacking, art, and collaboration finally paying off.

Marc kicks off a hub for Retro XP’s Wii 20th-anniversary coverage, basically planting the flag for a full celebration of Nintendo’s motion-control era.

Wilhelm tracks Fantasy Critic League’s week 44 shakeups as Phantom Blade Zero lands strong, One Piece: Grand Gourmet slips, and Shawn still can’t climb the standings.

The Chronicler reports two happy, exhausting days at SPIEL Essen 2026 packed with demos, booth visits, surprise finds, and plenty of board-game talk.

Ghastly lines up a spooky backlog with World of Warcraft’s Hallow’s End on Chromiecraft and the vampire RPG Cabernet stealing the show.

Tofutush’s October was low-key but busy enough: Minecraft glowstone grinding, a restarted conlang, a digital orrery, and signing next year’s apartment lease.

Juhis recaps a slower Djangonaut week of DjangoGirls PRs, pytest sessions, CI weirdness, and an RSVP-status bug fix still carrying into next week.

Bruce Schneier points to an eye-popping spike in AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and sums it up plainly: software security has entered a new world.

Axxuy is doing a personal November writing challenge, aiming for 10,000 blog words since NaNoWriMo is gone but the urge to write isn’t.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 1 November 2026
item.description:
Anarchae’s Divinity: Original Sin 2 diary covers smashing Magisters at Fort Joy, odd Ifan aggro, and the usual mountain of inventory management.

Aywren shares a Halloween-themed FFXIV update video, with love for All Saints’ Wake and hanging out in Sneaky Hollow.

Syp is enjoying LOTRO’s Wolves of Mordor as a scenic, lava-filled distraction with new zones, survival mechanics, and mysteries about Sauron’s wolf army.

Frostilyte argues Steam Next Fest wasn’t ruined by AI slop so much as overwhelmed by sheer scale and too many hopeful devs.

Magi gripes about AI-clogged Steam Next Fest, then highlights actual indie gems like Towers of Babble with help from smarter filtering tools.

Ellie digs into The Exit 8 as a sharp piece of liminal horror, tapping backrooms unease and anomaly-spotting for its creepy hook.

Wilhelm rounds up WordPress theme chaos, PHP2Shell jitters, classic editor nonsense, and a few gaming callbacks while crossing the 8,000-post mark.

Tobold says Frosthaven Digital’s 1.0 finally fixes onboarding with a gentler prequel campaign, even if the difficulty options still feel awkward.

Andrew Plotkin releases Visible Enchanter for everyone, with source code, manual scans, and some sharp appreciation for Enchanter’s story-first design.

Warner is taking Sunday Morning Reading off this week after Halloween with the grandkids, with a promise to return next Sunday.

Owls gives a tasty Chicago food crawl, from stress-ordering Milly’s pizza to a much-improved brunch at Creepies.

Cristian pushes back on Sam Altman’s cloud-first vision, arguing cloud platforms mainly want your data, not to help users.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 31 October 2026
item.description:
Margot’s Heart of Neon takeaway is less retro-game history than Jeff Minter’s warmth, creativity, and the human communities built around his work.

Wilhelm revisits Art of Rally and spots Over the Hill’s DNA everywhere, even if his own rally runs still end in trees and cautious grandma corners.

Anarchae juggles retail shift anxiety, murder mysteries, Vincent Price, Traitors rankings, sports watching, Fate/GO grinding, and DOS2 progress.

Heartless is happy to bank an ugly Packers win over the Panthers, especially since scoring 27 means an old meme gets another lap.

Bhagpuss reflects on music-post curation, half-remembered YouTube finds, and why discovery still matters even when the tunes barely stick.

Ramen Junkie checks out Beast Box Jetstream, a smaller transforming penguin with tight joints, neat articulation, and a surprisingly fiddly cube conversion.

Jimmy points readers to a fresh Analog Antiquarian post, this time a London-themed detour in his companion site’s worldly-wonders lane.

Jeff cheers UTC killing leap seconds, mainly because a first-ever negative leap second sounded like a great way to break computers everywhere.

Mike wraps RetroChallenge by teaching CamelForth some Halloween tricks, wrangling TMS9918A sprites, loops, and pumpkins onto the Sega SG-1000.

Tim Bray argues CoSocial’s paid, Canadian Mastodon co-op shows how decentralized social media can stay sane, transparent, and mostly troll-free.

Dave Winer jumps from dog-training videos and Claude to blogging, democracy, Google, ChatGPT art, and sports congratulations in classic stream form.

Emily says reading all the Bridgerton books only pushed her further from the show, mostly over its adaptation changes and casting choices.
